answer: The "Token Curated Registry" (TCR) mechanism resists Sybil attacks by requiring participants to stake a token on proposed entries, which are then voted on by a diverse group of curators. Each curator has a limited number of votes, analogous to a quill with a limited number of ink loads. As curators gain reputation, their votes carry more weight, like adding pigment to a painting. However, a Sybil attacker would need to stake a large amount of tokens, equivalent to building a terrace of high-value assets, making the attack economically unfeasible.
